annotations.title: Grouped Stage 2 removes the route-private traffic excess
annotations.note: PMC measures 1.447M TCC requests and 1.378M misses, down from 1.758M/1.509M for token-wave route-private GEMM2 and slightly below forced f16in at 1.478M/1.388M. The deterministic Stage-1 rank/leader mapping successfully restores duplicate-expert reuse.

annotations.title: Grouped active waves average 20.3k cycles
annotations.note: The active grouped waves average 20.35k cycles, close to forced f16in GEMM2's 18.89k and far below the 48.82k route-private token-wave waves. End-to-end Stage 2 is approximately 26.2 us.

annotations.title: Grouped GEMM2 is now limited by barrier and final memory waits
annotations.note: The largest aggregate costs are the final barrier at idx 482, the vmcnt(0) wait at idx 246, and barriers at idx 344/361. These are inherited from the grouped GEMM2 body, but the complete stage is already slightly faster than forced f16in GEMM2.
annotations.suggestion: Do not prioritize this until GEMM1 is improved; even eliminating these costs cannot remove the current full-pipeline gap.

annotations.title: Grouped GEMM2 inherits the baseline LDS conflict pattern
annotations.note: The grouped kernel records the same 63.75% LDS conflict ratio as the baseline GEMM2 body. Despite that, its traffic and latency are competitive. This remains an upstream kernel opportunity, not the reason the token-wave pipeline trails at M=16.
